terminus.sourceSays: The fall-prevention work team entered a household to address a bounded safety problem, but closer inspection connected the immediate fall risk to lighting, drainage, broken hot-water equipment, long-established bathing habits, fear of repair risk, family/community/state responsibility, and relationship work. The note explicitly says that what looks local can become an overall problem.
terminus.method: counterexample-driven synthesis against the prior portability/legibility model
terminus.generated: MUTHER candidate: LEGIBILITY CASCADE. Recognition interfaces do not only make latent capacities legible; they can also make hidden dependencies and failures legible. Once an intervention crosses a household/system boundary, each newly recognized dependency can enlarge the intervention scope: target problem -> linked infrastructure/habit -> trust/risk -> coordination/governance. Therefore better diagnosis can paradoxically increase, not reduce, the apparent size of the problem.
terminus.novelty: adds a recursive scope-expansion mechanism; not a summary of the source and not attributed to the source author
terminus.counterexampleNeed: seek a case where better diagnosis successfully narrows scope rather than expanding it, and a non-care domain where the cascade appears
